english.notes:
(i) Section 19(2) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 provides that revenue and customs information relating to a person means information about, acquired as a result of, or held in connection with the exercise of a function of the Revenue and Customs (within the meaning given by section 18(4)(c)) in respect of the person; but does not include information about internal administrative arrangements of His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (whether relating to Commissioners, officers or others).
(ii) Section 19(3) of the Act provides that it is a defence for a person charged with this offence of disclosing information to prove that he reasonably believed
(a) that the disclosure was lawful, OR
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(iii) Section 18(1) of the Act provides that Revenue and Customs officials may not disclose information which is held by the Revenue and Customs in connection with functions of the Revenue and Customs.
(iv) Section 20(9) of the Act provides that information disclosed in reliance on section 20 (public interest disclosure) may not be further disclosed without the consent of the Commissioners.
(v) A prosecution for this offence may be instituted only by the Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, section 19(5).
(vi) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the notes to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 55(1) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
